newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: GOLF-WESTNER AND MCNULTY FAVOURED FOR S.A. MASTERS.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-WESTNER AND MCNULTY FAVOURED FOR S.A. MASTERS.

text.p: Defending champion Wayne Westner and Zimbabwe's Mark McNulty are the players to beat in the 1997 South African Masters which starts at San Lameer Country Club near Port Edward on Thursday.
The big-hitting Westner, who has always produced golf of a high quality on South Africa's coastal courses, won last year's championship by three shots in very soggy conditions over the par-72 layout.

From there, Westner proceeded to win two more events on the South African tour -- both of them on the Indian Ocean coastline -- on his way to securing number one spot on the final FNB tour Order of Merit.

The 35-year-old, in partnership with world number four Ernie Els, then rounded off arguably the most successful year of his career with South Africa's memorable team victory in the World Cup of Golf at Erinvale.
Refreshed after a Christmas break, a confident Westner will therefore start as a leading contender and the proven form man over the 6,104-metre course in a field of 144 for the S.A. Masters title.
But, in McNulty, he will face a quality player who also enjoyed a highly successful 1996 season.

McNulty, always a consistent performer on the Southern African tour, finished fifth on the European tour Order of Merit last year with wins in the Dimension-Data tournament in South Africa, the Dutch Open and the prestigious Volvo Masters in Spain.
The smooth-swinging Zimbabwean then closed the year with a four-shot victory in his native country's open championship at Chapman Golf Club in Harare.
Like Westner, McNulty has since been recharging his golfing batteries over the New Year and an effective head-to-head duel between the two is highly likely at San Lameer this week.

Both are astute golfers in the coastal winds which are sure to whip up over the tight and heavily-watered layout and they are the biggest names in a field without the likes of Els, world number 13 Nick Price of Zimbabwe and South Africa's David Frost.
Yet there are several other players in Thursday's first round draw with genuine winning credentials.

Namibia's Trevor Dodds, a former campaigner on the U.S. tour, won on the Canadian circuit last year while South Africans Nico van Rensburg (sponsors invite), last year's Royal Swazi Classic champion Richard Kaplan and Craig Kamps, a pre-qualifier, have all tasted success in Asia.

Add the likes of Brenden Pappas, one of the leading players on last year's tour, 1995 S.A. Open champion Retief Goosen, former South African PGA champion Roger Wessels, 1994 S.A. Masters winner Chris Davison to the rapidly-emerging talents of Mark Muless, Brett Liddle, James Kingston and Warren Schutte and perhaps the 1997 South African Masters will not after all be the expected Westner-McNulty roadshow.
